holidays.name: National Heimlich Maneuver Day
holidays.description: A day to learn the abdominal-thrust technique that has rescued countless choking victims. Skip the dinner-party drama. Take a first-aid class and practice on a willing dummy instead.
holidays.origin: The day honors Dr. Henry Heimlich, the thoracic surgeon who introduced the technique to the public in the mid-1970s. It began as a way to promote choking-rescue awareness and basic first-aid training.
holidays.funFact: Before the Heimlich maneuver caught on, standard advice for choking victims often included back blows alone. Heimlich's technique was so popular that it became a household name within just a few years.

holidays.name: Flip a Coin Day
holidays.description: A day to settle your dilemmas the old-fashioned way: heads or tails. It covers everything from who picks the pizza topping to which road to take. Fate gets to be the boss for 24 hours.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the ancient tradition of using a coin toss to make fair, quick decisions.
holidays.funFact: A Stanford-led study of coin tossing found that a flipped coin lands on the same side it started on about 51% of the time. So if you can see which side is up before the flip, you get a tiny edge.

holidays.name: National Hazelnut Cake Day
holidays.description: A nutty, buttery celebration of one of the most elegant desserts. Bakers whip up layers of toasty hazelnut sponge, often with chocolate or praline frosting. Everyone else just shows up with a fork.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It gives dessert lovers an excuse to celebrate the rich, toasty flavor of hazelnuts in cake form.
holidays.funFact: Turkey grows most of the world's hazelnuts, and the nuts have been cultivated around the Black Sea region for thousands of years.
